content:
The most dangerous workplace culture isn’t always the one where people are shouted at.

Sometimes, it’s the one where your work is recognised without your name.

Look at these two certificates.

In 2014, Tarachand Agencies, Chennai was recognised alongside multiple contributors Romech Kenne, Pige Suena, Viteam Siegh and Arita Ras.

The message was:

“This was a team effort.”

Then look at 2024.

The recognition is centred on one individual Nashmatti, Sales Director.

And that made me think about leadership.

A leader who constantly takes the spotlight away from their team may get the applause but gradually loses something far more important:

Trust.

Because hardworking people don’t necessarily leave organisations because the work is difficult.

Sometimes, they leave because they become tired of being invisible.

They contributed.
They delivered.
They stayed late.
They solved problems.
They helped build the success.

But when the applause comes, only one person is standing in the picture.

That’s not leadership.

Leadership is making your team visible even when you could take all the credit yourself.

A strong leader doesn’t feel threatened by talented people.

They put those people in the spotlight.

So here’s the question every leader should ask:

“When my team succeeds, am I trying to make myself look important or am I making sure the people who made it happen are recognised?”

Because your legacy isn’t the number of times your name appeared.

It’s the number of people whose names you helped put forward.

#Leadership #ToxicLeadership #WorkplaceCulture #EmployeeRecognition #LeadershipLessons #Teamwork #Management #EmployeeEngagement #PeopleFirst
comment: A useful test of leadership is what happens when the leader is absent. If recognition systems still highlight the contributors, the culture is likely stronger than one built around a single name.
